Rachel / team — thanks for the heads-up. Policy summary and recommendation below.

Policy baseline: Redwood requires POs for vendor onboarding for standard engagements. Exceptions are permitted for low-dollar pilots or situations where the customer cannot issue POs quickly, subject to procurement approval and controls. Standard controls we require for an invoice-only exception:
- Max duration: 90 days (can be shortened)
- Spend cap without PO: $25,000 total during exception window
- Required artifacts: completed W-9, billing contact, evidence of procurement constraint (they provided), and either a signed MSA or a short-term invoice agreement signed via DocuSign
- Payment terms: Net 30 by default; finance can consider Net 45 case-by-case with justification
- AP process: flag invoices with "TEMP-INVOICE-EX" tag so AP routes for manual validation

For SummitLogic specifically (pilot ~$6k): I recommend granting a 90-day invoice-only exception up to $25k, provided we get the W-9 and a signed temporary invoice agreement. We should also require an internal customer contact to own approvals and confirm invoices match pilot usage.

I've attached a short template we use for temporary exceptions: Redwood-temp-invoice-agreement.docx

Next steps I suggest:
1) Rachel: confirm billing contact & cadence with Jason
2) Marissa: open PROC ticket and flag AP for manual routing (I'll create PROC-3421)
3) Karthik / Naomi / Sean: any comments on insurance/cert requirements or additional controls?
